[ THE PROBLEM ]

The battlefield changed faster than the defense industry could respond. One-way FPV attack drones — assembled for hundreds of dollars, flown at 30 m/s, swarmed in volume — now account for the majority of casualties in active conflict zones. Legacy C-sUAS systems were engineered for a different threat: large, slow, RF-dependent platforms at kilometer-scale ranges. They are too expensive, too heavy, and too slow for the fight that's actually happening at 50 meters.

Counter-drone built for speed, and close-in engagements.
